title: ChatGPT’s teen mode may weaken adolescents’ sense of independence
teaser: In August, OpenAI launched Teen Mode, a ChatGPT setting that automatically applies to all users under 18. It came a year after a lawsuit alleged that ChatGPT contributed to the suicide of 16-year-old Adam Raine. The mode restricts access to dangerous content, notifies parents when it detects signs of self-harm, and prevents the chatbot from presenting itself as a friend. But psychoanalyst Robin Kirman believes that even a study tool within Teen Mode could harm adolescents’ development: constant AI assistance may make it harder for them to form their own opinions and trust their own feelings.
